answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed when peers prove fraud. An attacker who wants to wander through the market under a thousand fresh names must fund each one, so the delta between the cost of one honest identity and a Sybil swarm grows with every clone. Reputation then accrues slowly, like onyx forming layer by layer, and cannot be bought in bulk: each new identity starts at zero trust and must earn its way up, so flooding the economy costs far more than it can ever return.
